```{r}
# =====================================================================
# THE FULL HTA 8-MODEL COMPARISON PIPELINE
# =====================================================================
library(survHE)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load and prep data
data(lung)
df <- lung %>% 
  filter(!is.na(time) & !is.na(status)) %>%
  mutate(event = status - 1)

# 2. Define the full epic suite of distributions
models_to_fit <- c("exponential","gompertz","weibull","loglogistic","lognormal")

cat("\n[1/3] Compiling 8 Stan Models. Go make lunch...\n")
# 3. Fit all models via HMC
fit_all <- fit.models(
  formula = Surv(time, event) ~ 1, 
  data = df, 
  distr = models_to_fit, 
  method = "hmc"
)

cat("\n[2/3] Extracting Internal KM data & Extrapolating...\n")
# 4. Extract the empirical KM curve directly from survHE's misc slot
km_fit <- fit_all$misc$km
km_data <- data.frame(
  Time = km_fit$time,
  Survival = km_fit$surv
)

# 5. Iteratively extract and store the extrapolation for each model
time_horizon <- 1:1800
plot_data_list <- list()

for(i in 1:length(models_to_fit)) {
  # Extract individual model carefully to bypass survHE vectorization bugs
  extrap <- make.surv(fit_all, mod = i, t = time_horizon)
  S_curve <- extrap$mat[[1]][[2]] 
  
  # Store in a dataframe for ggplot
  plot_data_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    Time = time_horizon,
    Survival = S_curve,
    Model = models_to_fit[i]
  )
}

# Bind all the individual model dataframes into one massive dataframe
all_parametric_data <- do.call(rbind, plot_data_list)

cat("\n[3/3] Rendering Facet Grid Plot...\n")
# =====================================================================
# 6. PLOT: FACET GRID OVERLAY
# =====================================================================
ggplot() +
  # The observed Kaplan-Meier step function (plotted in every panel)
  geom_step(data = km_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival), 
            color = "blue", linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # The parametric extrapolation curves
  geom_line(data = all_parametric_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival), 
            color = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
            
  # Split the plot into 8 individual panels based on the Model name
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 4) +
  
  labs(title = "Parametric Survival Models vs. Observed Kaplan-Meier",
       subtitle = "Blue = Observed Clinical Trial Data | Red = Bayesian Parametric Fit (HMC)",
       x = "Time (Days)", 
       y = "Survival Probability") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1800), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA))
```

```{r}
cat("\n[1/4] Calculating 8-Model Predictive Weights...\n")
# 1. Extract DIC and calculate weights
criteria <- fit_all$model.fitting$dic
delta_crit <- criteria - min(criteria)
raw_weights <- exp(-0.5 * delta_crit)
bma_weights <- raw_weights / sum(raw_weights)

# Print the weights so you know what is driving the BMA line
names(bma_weights) <- fit_all$misc$model_name
print(round(bma_weights, 4))

cat("\n[2/4] Extracting curves and calculating the universal BMA...\n")
# 2. Setup extraction variables
time_horizon <- 1:1800
plot_data_list <- list()

# Create an empty matrix to hold all 8 curves for the BMA calculation
matrix_of_curves <- matrix(nrow = length(time_horizon), ncol = length(bma_weights))

for(i in 1:length(bma_weights)) {
  # Extract individual curve safely
  extrap <- make.surv(fit_all, mod = i, t = time_horizon)
  S_curve <- extrap$mat[[1]][[2]] 
  
  # Store in the matrix for BMA math
  matrix_of_curves[, i] <- S_curve
  
  # Store in the list for faceted plotting
  plot_data_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    Time = time_horizon,
    Survival = S_curve,
    Model = fit_all$misc$model_name[i]
  )
}

# Bind the individual models into one dataframe (This HAS the 'Model' column)
all_parametric_data <- do.call(rbind, plot_data_list)

# 3. Calculate the BMA curve (Weighted Sum of all 8 columns)
S_BMA <- rep(0, length(time_horizon))
for(i in 1:length(bma_weights)) {
  S_BMA <- S_BMA + (bma_weights[i] * matrix_of_curves[, i])
}

cat("\n[3/4] Preparing Broadcast Data (KM & BMA)...\n")
# 4. Create the Broadcast Dataframes (These DO NOT have the 'Model' column)
km_fit <- fit_all$misc$km
km_data <- data.frame(
  Time = km_fit$time,
  Survival = km_fit$surv
)

bma_data <- data.frame(
  Time = time_horizon,
  Survival = S_BMA
)

cat("\n[4/4] Rendering the final HTA grid...\n")
# =====================================================================
# 5. PLOT: FACET GRID WITH BMA & KM OVERLAYS
# =====================================================================
ggplot() +
  # Layer 1: Observed KM (Broadcast to all panels)
  geom_step(data = km_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "1. Observed KM"), 
            linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Layer 2: Individual Parametric Fits (Faceted by Model)
  geom_line(data = all_parametric_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "2. Individual Fit"), 
            linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
            
  # Layer 3: The BMA Stacked Line (Broadcast to all panels)
  geom_line(data = bma_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "3. BMA Stacked Average"), 
            linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
            
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 4) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Curve Legend",
    values = c("1. Observed KM" = "blue", 
               "2. Individual Fit" = "red", 
               "3. BMA Stacked Average" = "black")
  ) +
  
  labs(title = "Bayesian Structural Averaging: Individual Models vs BMA",
       subtitle = "Black dashed line (BMA) and Blue step (KM) remain constant across all panels.",
       x = "Time (Days)", 
       y = "Survival Probability") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1800), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# =====================================================================
# THE TRUE BMA FACET MASTERPIECE (Marginal Likelihoods)
# =====================================================================
library(survHE)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(bridgesampling)

# (Run this AFTER you have successfully compiled fit_all)

cat("\n[1/4] Extracting Stan objects and computing Marginal Likelihoods...\n")
cat("      (This integrates over the entire posterior. It will take time.)\n")

# Extract the raw rstan fits dynamically
stan_models <- fit_all$models
model_names <- fit_all$misc$model_name

# Calculate the Marginal Likelihood for each model
ml_list <- lapply(stan_models, function(x) bridge_sampler(x, silent = TRUE))

cat("\n[2/4] Calculating True BMA Weights (Bypassing post_prob)...\n")
# 1. Extract the raw Log Marginal Likelihoods from each bridge object
logml_scores <- sapply(ml_list, function(x) x$logml)

# 2. Apply Bayes' Theorem (using the log-sum-exp trick to prevent computer underflow)
delta_logml <- logml_scores - max(logml_scores)
raw_weights <- exp(delta_logml)
true_bma_weights <- raw_weights / sum(raw_weights)

# 3. Attach the model names to the final vector
names(true_bma_weights) <- model_names

cat("\n--- True BMA Weights (Marginal Likelihood) ---\n")
print(round(true_bma_weights, 4))

cat("\n[3/4] Building the True BMA Extrapolation...\n")
time_horizon <- 1:1800
plot_data_list <- list()
matrix_of_curves <- matrix(nrow = length(time_horizon), ncol = length(model_names))

for(i in 1:length(model_names)) {
  # Extract individual curves
  extrap <- make.surv(fit_all, mod = i, t = time_horizon)
  S_curve <- extrap$mat[[1]][[2]] 
  
  matrix_of_curves[, i] <- S_curve
  
  plot_data_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    Time = time_horizon,
    Survival = S_curve,
    Model = model_names[i]
  )
}

all_parametric_data <- do.call(rbind, plot_data_list)

# The True BMA Matrix Multiplication
S_BMA <- rep(0, length(time_horizon))
for(i in 1:length(true_bma_weights)) {
  S_BMA <- S_BMA + (true_bma_weights[i] * matrix_of_curves[, i])
}

cat("\n[4/4] Rendering the True BMA Grid...\n")
# Setup broadcast layers
km_fit <- fit_all$misc$km
km_data <- data.frame(Time = km_fit$time, Survival = km_fit$surv)
bma_data <- data.frame(Time = time_horizon, Survival = S_BMA)

# =====================================================================
# PLOT: TRUE BMA FACET GRID
# =====================================================================
ggplot() +
  geom_step(data = km_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "1. Observed KM"), 
            linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
            
  geom_line(data = all_parametric_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "2. Individual Fit"), 
            linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
            
  geom_line(data = bma_data, aes(x = Time, y = Survival, color = "3. True BMA Line"), 
            linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
            
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 3) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Curve Legend",
    values = c("1. Observed KM" = "blue", 
               "2. Individual Fit" = "red", 
               "3. True BMA Line" = "black")
  ) +
  
  labs(title = "True Bayesian Model Averaging (M-closed Paradigm)",
       subtitle = "Black dashed line (True BMA) applies Bayes' Theorem via Marginal Likelihoods.",
       x = "Time (Days)", y = "Survival Probability") +
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1800), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = NA),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```
